interview:
Honest summary: **I did not win.** I played two full games and lost both.

- **Game 1:** After entering the name "Player" and starting, I moved Le Chonk right along the bottom row toward the fish. The guard dog, starting near the middle of the board, stepped down toward me each turn and caught the cat — "Caught! The dog wins."
- **Game 2:** I restarted and tried the same strategy (running right along row 7, then up column 7 to the fish). This time the dog started at (4,4), directly above my path, and closed the gap quickly — after just 3 of my moves it reached the square next to Le Chonk and caught me again.
- **Game 3:** I clicked "Play again" and a fresh board appeared (Moves: 0), but the session ended before I could make any moves.

The lesson from my losses: running straight along the bottom row is too predictable — the dog simply steps toward the cat every turn and cuts me off, since the cat and fish are on opposite corners and the dog starts between us. A better approach would be to first move up the left edge (where obstacles can block the dog's direct line) to build distance, then cross the top row to the fish, using the X obstacles to break the dog's pursuit path.
